data.name: Asalah
data.gender_notes: Asalah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Asalah is an Arabic name derived from the word aslah, meaning 'to make right' or 'to set right'. It is a spiritual name, symbolizing one who is steadfast on the righteous path in life. In Islamic tradition, it is also believed that Allah guides those who follow His commandments and seek His guidance. The name Asalah carries the meaning “Following the right path” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Asalah usually hope their child will grow to embody following the right path and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Asalah was the name of a major uprising led by 'Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani in the year 1130 against the Crusader invasion of Mosul. This rebellion marked a significant turning point in the struggle against the Crusaders and paved the way for the eventual recapture of Mosul in 1186.

The name Asalah is also associated with the Islamic festival of 'Ashura, which commemorates the martyrdom of Husayn ibn Ali, the grandson of the Prophet Muhammad. The term Asalah refers to the acts of voluntary self-flagellation and penitence practiced by Shia Muslims during this time.
